scenes.headline: When does the AI bubble burst?
scenes.detail: A striking valuation. A harder question about returns.
scenes.voiceover: One point seven seven trillion dollars. That was Anthropic's fully diluted valuation at its market debut.

claims.text: Anthropic debut-day fully diluted valuation approximately $1.77T

scenes.headline: One day changes the mood
scenes.detail: Reuters intraday snapshot, not the closing price.
scenes.voiceover: By the following day, shares were under pressure. So is this the moment the bubble bursts?

scenes.headline: Demand is real
scenes.detail: Reported Q3 revenue, up 47 percent quarter on quarter.
scenes.voiceover: The bull case begins with real demand. The Claude maker reported almost seventeen billion dollars in quarterly revenue, up forty seven percent from the previous quarter.

scenes.headline: But what price?
scenes.detail: Reuters estimate of trailing sales multiple; market-sensitive.
scenes.voiceover: But investors were paying roughly forty times trailing sales. That valuation leaves little room for disappointment.

claims.text: Approximately 40 times trailing sales according to Reuters

scenes.headline: The buildout costs trillions
scenes.detail: ECB estimate: cumulative US Big Tech capital expenditure through 2030.
scenes.voiceover: And the European Central Bank estimates that United States big tech could invest five point five trillion dollars by twenty thirty.

claims.text: ECB projection of US Big Tech cumulative capex of about $5.5T through 2030

scenes.headline: Two very different futures

left.label: BULL CASE
left.body: Paying customers scale as cost per AI task declines.

right.label: BEAR CASE
right.body: Growth slows before power, chips and debt can be repaid.

scenes.voiceover: The optimists see faster adoption and cheaper computing. The skeptics see slower growth, expensive chips and debt commitments.

claims.text: Faster adoption and improving unit economics could sustain returns
claims.qualifier: Illustrative bull scenario, not a forecast

claims.text: Slower growth and expensive commitments could compress valuation
claims.qualifier: Illustrative bear scenario, not a forecast

scenes.headline: Technology is not the stock price
scenes.detail: No credible source can name the day a market bubble bursts.
scenes.voiceover: A stock market correction would not mean artificial intelligence has failed. No one can name the exact day the bubble bursts. Watch cash flow. And watch the gap between promise and price.

claims.text: A stock-market correction is distinct from technology adoption
